world.title: Putin 'ready' to accept Nato-like shield for Ukraine, but with a catch
world.summary: President Vladimir Putin expressed willingness to accept a NATO-like security arrangement for Ukraine, contingent on specific conditions. This statement follows Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, which was justified by Moscow as a response to Ukraine's aspirations to join NATO, perceived as a significant threat to Russian national security. The proposal remains under discussion amid ongoing tensions.

world.title: Indian-origin couple killed in targeted shooting outside Canada Walmart
world.summary: A 23-year-old Indian-origin man and his 24-year-old girlfriend were shot dead outside a Walmart in Surrey, British Columbia. Canadian investigators suspect the shooting was a targeted attack related to organized crime. They are examining a burnt vehicle found nearby as part of their investigation. The incident has raised concerns about safety and crime in the area.

world.title: Bullets rain from helicopter, explosions on ground: How Mexico hunted down FBI's most-wanted drug lord; watch
world.summary: Mexican authorities captured Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, an FBI-listed drug lord, in Sinaloa, resulting in intense gun battles and explosions. The operation unfolded near a baseball stadium, causing widespread panic among spectators. The confrontation involved military forces and marked a significant moment in Mexico's ongoing efforts to combat drug trafficking and apprehend high-profile criminals linked to organized crime.

business.title: 'I spend Rs 20,000 on shared 2BHK': 28-year-old woman breaks down cost of living in Bengaluru
business.summary: A 28-year-old woman detailed her monthly budget for living in Bengaluru, highlighting expenses such as rent, groceries, food delivery, and transportation. She spends Rs 20,000 on a shared 2BHK apartment, prompting discussions about the high cost of living in the city. Her video illustrates the financial challenges faced by young professionals in urban environments.

business.title: "Pee On Your Brain": Report Claims Jensen Huang's 'Culture Of Fear' At Nvidia
business.summary: A report alleges that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang fosters a "culture of fear" within the company, characterized by public criticism, personal insults, and threats towards employees. This leadership style has come under scrutiny as Nvidia has grown into one of the world's most valuable tech firms. Huang's personal life has also attracted media attention for extramarital affairs.

business.title: Harley-Davidson Sprint 440 Launched in Japan, India Next?
business.summary: Harley-Davidson has launched the Sprint 440 motorcycle in Japan, developed in collaboration with its Indian partner, Hero MotoCorp. This model is the second motorcycle resulting from their partnership. The Sprint 440 made its world premiere at EICMA 2026 and is expected to be available in India soon, following its introduction in the Japanese market.

technology.title: HydraSure’s Gen Z Team Turns GTA VI Launch Day Into a Giveaway
technology.summary: HydraSure, a hydration brand from Antila Lifesciences Private Limited, is celebrating the global launch of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) with a social media giveaway. Announced on launch day, the initiative offers two winners a chance to win copies of the game: one will receive the Ultimate Edition, while the other will receive the Standard Edition.

technology.title: HydraSure’s Gen Z Team Turns GTA VI Launch Day Into a Giveaway - Planned and Live in 24 Hours
technology.summary: HydraSure, a hydration brand from Antila Lifesciences, launched a social media giveaway coinciding with the global release of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI). The initiative was conceptualized and executed by the company's Gen Z team within 24 hours, highlighting their agility in responding to trending events. The campaign aims to engage fans and enhance brand visibility.

technology.title: Apple plans autonomous AI agent to take on OpenAI and Meta, but could its iPhone ecosystem give it an edge?
technology.summary: Apple is reportedly developing an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, controlling apps, and completing complex tasks. This initiative aims to enhance its competitive position against companies like OpenAI and Meta. The strength of Apple's iPhone ecosystem and its emphasis on privacy may provide a significant advantage in the rapidly evolving artificial intelligence landscape.

sports.title: Nadal’s presentation, the Negreira Case, budget, and everything you need to know about today’s General Assembly
sports.summary: Rafa Nadal attended a General Assembly at Valdebebas, accompanied by honorary president Pirri. The event featured the anthem of La Décima, with 758 Real Madrid members present. Florentino Pérez defended member ownership and addressed the Negreira case, challenging LaLiga. The assembly highlighted key issues, including budget discussions and the ongoing situation surrounding the Negreira controversy.

sports.title: 'We all made mistakes': Darren Lehmann stands by Sandpapergate version, reveals 'dark place' after 2018 scandal
sports.summary: Darren Lehmann, former Australian cricket coach, reiterated his lack of knowledge regarding the Sandpapergate scandal, which occurred in 2018. He acknowledged that mistakes were made by all involved and described the aftermath as a "dark place" for him personally. The controversy continues to affect Australian cricket, with Lehmann's comments drawing renewed attention to the incident.

sports.title: Mushfiqur Rahim ruled out of second South Africa Test
sports.summary: Bangladesh's veteran batter Mushfiqur Rahim has been ruled out of the second Test against South Africa due to a groin injury. This absence is a significant setback for the team as they prepare for the match, which is scheduled to take place at Centurion on November 23. Rahim's experience will be missed in the lineup.

health.title: A pill that makes pancreatic cancer disappear? What the daraxonrasib trial found
health.summary: An experimental pill, daraxonrasib, has demonstrated promising results in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer by targeting KRAS mutations. Dr. Parveen Jain, Senior Consultant at Aakash Healthcare, discusses how this treatment differs from conventional chemotherapy and its potential implications for future therapies. Early findings suggest it may offer new hope for patients facing this challenging diagnosis.

health.title: Repeated CT scans, MRIs may raise brain tumour risk-what study of 3.7 mn US, Canadian children found
health.summary: A study involving 3.7 million children in the US and Canada suggests that repeated CT scans and MRIs may increase the risk of brain tumors. This finding aligns with similar research from the UK and Australia, indicating a link between radiation exposure from medical imaging and heightened cancer risk. Authors recommend limiting such imaging to necessary clinical situations.

health.title: Blood sugar spikes: Why the same meal may affect you differently at breakfast and dinner
health.summary: Research indicates that the same meal can lead to different blood sugar spikes at breakfast and dinner due to variations in insulin sensitivity. An endocrinologist explains that insulin sensitivity is generally higher in the morning and decreases throughout the day. This suggests that the body processes carbohydrates more effectively earlier, impacting blood sugar responses based on meal timing.

science.title: What other planets smell like according to chemistry
science.summary: Physics professor Boyko Ranguelov discusses the potential odors of various planets based on their chemical compositions. Gas giants are suggested to smell like rotten eggs, while Mars is described as having a rust-like scent due to its high iron content. Although direct experience of these planetary smells is impossible, scientific analysis provides insights into their likely odors.

science.title: NASA's Curiosity Rover Spots Potato Chip-Shaped Rocks On Mars
science.summary: NASA's Curiosity Rover has discovered unusual rock formations on Mars resembling potato chips. Located at the Nazca site, these disk-shaped structures feature curled and uneven shapes embedded in the bedrock. Scientists are investigating the origins and development of these formations to gain insights into Mars' geological history and the processes that shaped its surface.

science.title: Scientists Develop New Method to Control Magnetisation for Quantum Information Storage
science.summary: On November 20, 2026, researchers at the Raman Research Institute in Bengaluru introduced a theoretical method to control quantum magnetism by modifying network connectivity. This innovative approach aims to facilitate the engineering of entangled quantum states, which are essential for advancements in quantum information storage. The development holds potential implications for future quantum computing technologies and applications.

entertainment.title: 'Brad Pitt of Bihar' Ravi Kishan teaches Akshay Kumar his viral hookstep on 'Koffee With Karan 9'; duo turns the couch into a dance floor - Watch
entertainment.summary: Akshay Kumar and actor-politician Ravi Kishan will appear together on Season 9 of Karan Johar's chat show 'Koffee With Karan.' A new promo showcases their entertaining episode, featuring humor, engaging conversation, and an impromptu dance session. Ravi Kishan, dubbed the 'Brad Pitt of Bihar,' teaches Akshay his viral hookstep, transforming the couch into a lively dance floor.

entertainment.title: Diljit Dosanjh's Ahmedabad concert faces objection over four songs, Dr Pandit Rao Dharennavar warns: 'If he performs these songs, I will approach the Gujarat High Court and file a contempt of court ca
entertainment.summary: Diljit Dosanjh's upcoming concert at Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad faces objections over four songs in his setlist. Dr. Pandit Rao Dharennavar, a Chandigarh-based academic, has requested the singer to remove these songs. He has warned that if the songs are performed, he will approach the Gujarat High Court to file a contempt of court case.

entertainment.title: After Indore, Diljit Dosanjh warned of contempt plea over ‘Patiala Peg’, ‘5 Tara Theke’, 2 other songs in Ahmedabad
entertainment.summary: Ahead of Diljit Dosanjh's concert at Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, Dr. Dharennavar, an associate professor at PGGC-46, Chandigarh, has raised concerns over the performance of specific songs including 'Patiala Peg', 'Panj Tara', 'Je Bichcho Feem Labbiya', and 'Jatt Utthe Fire Karda'. He warned of a contempt plea if these songs are performed during the event.
